mainTopic: רבי עקיבא's view in the משנה about fixing a מבוי, the identity of the תלמיד as רבי מאיר, and the laws of קנקנתום ink and the סוטה scroll
overview: The גמרא starts with רבי עקיבא's line in the משנה: בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about every מבוי, even a narrow one. It asks how this differs from the תנא קמא, and answers that they differ over רב אחלי's rule, though we do not know who holds which side. A ברייתא has רבי עקיבא say that the תלמיד, not רבי ישמעאל, made the statement, and that the הלכה follows him. Two answers explain this apparent contradiction: שמואל says it was only to sharpen the students, and רב נחמן בר יצחק says the wording was 'his words appear reasonable'. רבי יהושע בן לוי identifies the unnamed תלמיד as רבי מאיר, who served both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא. Two stories about רבי מאיר's קנקנתום ink disagree about the order of his teachers and about who forbade the ink. The order is resolved, but who forbade the ink stays an unanswered קשיא. The גמרא then discusses using קנקנתום everywhere except פרשת סוטה, and whether a סוטה passage may be erased from a ספר תורה. It ties this to a dispute about reusing one סוטה's scroll for another, but רב פפא and רב נחמן בר יצחק push back on that link. The amud ends as the גמרא begins a challenge to רבי אחי בר יאשיה from a משנה about a גט, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא says they argue in both cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line of the משנה where רבי עקיבא rejects the תלמיד's limit on the dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: They disagree about this case and about that case, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the words of the משנה it is about to discuss. It is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תלמיד said בית שמאי and בית הלל argue only about a מבוי four to ten אמות wide, and a narrower one needs nothing. רבי עקיבא disagrees and says they argue about the narrow מבוי too. So in his view even a מבוי under four אמות needs a fix.

keyTerms.meaning: About this and about that, meaning both cases
They disagreed
Etc., used when only the opening words of a quote are given
An alleyway that the courtyards open into

steps.confusionAlert: 'This and that' does not mean two different topics. It means both widths of מבוי: under four אמות, and four to ten אמות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:

phrases.aramaic: עַל זֶה וְעַל זֶה נֶחְלְקוּ כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: They disagree about this and about that, etc.
phrases.notes: About a narrow alleyway (under four cubits) and a wider one (four to ten cubits).

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening quote from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about every מבוי, even one narrower than four אמות.

steps.title: Isn't רבי עקיבא the same as the תנא קמא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי עקיבא's view is recorded separately, since it seems to match the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא's view is the same as the תנא קמא's!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. It asks why רבי עקיבא needs to be quoted, since his view sounds the same as the opening statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא stated the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל without any limit, so it seems to cover every מבוי. רבי עקיבא also says they argue in every case. If the two views are the same, there is no reason to record them as separate opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as
The first תנא, the unnamed opening opinion in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The תנא קמא here is the opening, unnamed statement of the dispute. It is not the תלמיד who quoted רבי ישמעאל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva
is the same as the first Tanna!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the רבי עקיבא line quoted in Step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's decision to record רבי עקיבא's view as a separate opinion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two opinions that say the same thing should not be listed as separate views.

steps.title: They differ over רב אחלי's rule, but we don't know who holds which side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא and the תנא קמא disagree about רב אחלי's rule. It is not clear which of them accepts the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them regarding the rule of רב אחלי, and some say רב יחיאל. But it is not determined which one holds which view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by naming a practical difference between the two opinions. It then admits that we cannot tell which opinion holds which side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחלי, or some say רב יחיאל, taught that a מבוי less than four טפחים wide needs no fix at all. One of the two תנאים accepts this rule, and the other says even such a tiny מבוי needs a fix. So the views are truly different, but the גמרא cannot say which side each one takes.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
And some say, introducing another name for the same speaker
And they are not identified, meaning we do not know who holds which view

steps.confusionAlert: רב אחלי's measure is four טפחים (handbreadths). The תלמיד's measure is four אמות (cubits). These are two different sizes.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them regarding the rule of Rav Achlai,
phrases.notes: רב אחלי's rule: an alleyway less than four טפחים wide needs no fix.

phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Yechiel.
But it is not determined who holds which view.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a practical difference (נפקא מינה) between the two opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא and the תנא קמא seemed to say exactly the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: They disagree about whether a מבוי under four טפחים needs a fix, as רב אחלי taught. We do not know which תנא holds which side.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer shows that the גמרא can prove two opinions are different without knowing which side each one takes.

steps.title: ברייתא: the student said it, and the הלכה follows him
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי עקיבא saying the statement came from the תלמיד, not רבי ישמעאל, and that the הלכה follows the תלמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי עקיבא said, רבי ישמעאל did not say this. Rather, that student said this, and the הלכה follows that student.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with more information about the תלמיד in the משנה. This sets up the problem the גמרא will raise next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא says the תלמיד did not truly hear this from רבי ישמעאל and said it on his own. Yet in the same breath he rules that the הלכה follows that תלמיד. These two parts seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
This matter
That student
The practical law follows the view of...

phrases.english: It was taught in a Baraita: Rabbi Akiva said:

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל דָּבָר זֶה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael did not say this matter,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אוֹתוֹ תַּלְמִיד אָמַר דָּבָר זֶה,
phrases.english: rather, that student said this matter,
and the halacha follows that student.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source about the תלמיד from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, the statement came from the תלמיד and not from רבי ישמעאל, and the הלכה follows the תלמיד.

steps.title: The ברייתא contradicts itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא seems to reject the תלמיד's view and then rule like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא itself is difficult. You said 'רבי ישמעאל did not say this,' which implies the הלכה does not follow that view. Then you said 'the הלכה follows that student'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from Step 4 by showing that its first half and second half seem to contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'רבי ישמעאל did not say this' sounds like rejecting the view, as if so great a sage would never say something wrong. If the view is wrong, the הלכה should not follow it. Yet the ברייתא ends by ruling like the תלמיד, which is the opposite.

keyTerms.meaning: This statement itself is difficult, meaning it contradicts itself
You said
This proves, apparently
And then, afterward
The halacha does not follow him

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרַתְּ ״לָא אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל דָּבָר זֶה״ —
phrases.english: You said 'Rabbi Yishmael did not say this matter' —
apparently the halacha does not follow that view,
and then you said: 'The halacha follows that student'!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא גּוּפַהּ קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the internal consistency of the ברייתא quoted in Step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא of רבי עקיבא about the תלמיד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first half implies the view is rejected, but the second half rules like it. A single statement cannot say both.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא praised the student only to sharpen his students
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that רבי עקיבא did not really rule like the תלמיד. He said it only to encourage his students to think sharply.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: רבי עקיבא said this only to sharpen his students' minds with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to the contradiction from Step 5. רבי עקיבא's words 'the הלכה follows the תלמיד' were not a real ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that רבי עקיבא rejected the תלמיד's view and then ruled like him. שמואל says only the rejection was his true opinion. The praise was a teaching method, meant to encourage students to come up with fresh, sharp ideas.

keyTerms.meaning: to sharpen (the mind)
students
he only said it in order to

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'the הלכה follows the תלמיד' as a real ruling, according to this answer. רבי עקיבא's actual position stays that the תלמיד's limit is rejected.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Rabbi Akiva did not say it
phrases.notes: 'It' refers to the statement that the הלכה follows the תלמיד.

phrases.english: except to sharpen the students with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא אֲמָרָהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אֶלָּא לְחַדֵּד בָּהּ הַתַּלְמִידִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the purpose of a statement: the praise was a teaching tool, not a ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא both rejected the תלמיד's view and ruled like it, which is a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the rejection was his real view. The 'הלכה' line was meant to sharpen the students.

steps.title: The original wording was 'his words appear correct'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the ברייתא really said 'his words appear correct', not 'the הלכה follows him'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן בר יצחק said: 'They appear (reasonable)' was what was stated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to the same contradiction. It corrects the wording of רבי עקיבא's praise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב נחמן בר יצחק, רבי עקיבא never said 'the הלכה follows the תלמיד'. He only said the תלמיד's words seem logical. Calling an idea reasonable does not mean ruling like it, so the contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: they appear (correct or reasonable)
it was stated

phrases.english: And Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
'They appear reasonable' was what was stated.
phrases.notes: This replaces the wording 'the הלכה follows the תלמיד'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר נִרְאִין אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent answer to the contradiction in Step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says 'the הלכה follows the תלמיד'.
steps.terutzMaskana: It actually says the תלמיד's words 'appear reasonable', which is praise and not a ruling.

steps.title: The unnamed student is always רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that whenever a 'תלמיד' speaks before רבי עקיבא in the name of רבי ישמעאל, it is רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Anywhere you find 'A certain תלמיד said before רבי עקיבא in the name of רבי ישמעאל', it is none other than רבי מאיר, who served both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves to a new point: who this unnamed תלמיד actually is. רבי יהושע בן לוי gives a general rule identifying him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule uses the fact that only a student of both teachers could quote רבי ישמעאל to רבי עקיבא. רבי מאיר fits, because he served both of them. This statement sets up the proof that comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: anywhere that you find (introduces a general rule)
a certain student (unnamed)
served, attended (as a close student)
רבי מאיר, a תנא who was a student of רבי עקיבא

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule applies across ש״ס. Whenever you see this unnamed-student formula, you know the speaker is רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Anywhere that you find
'In the name of Rabbi Yishmael said'
'a certain student before Rabbi Akiva' —
it is none other than Rabbi Meir,
who served Rabbi Yishmael
and Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה מוֹצֵא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אָמַר תַּלְמִיד אֶחָד לִפְנֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from resolving the contradiction to identifying the unnamed תלמיד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The anonymous תלמיד who quotes רבי ישמעאל before רבי עקיבא is always רבי מאיר.

steps.title: Proof that רבי מאיר studied with both teachers
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר studied under both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא. This supports רבי יהושע בן לוי's identification.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי מאיר said: When I was with רבי ישמעאל, I used to put קנקנתום (iron sulfate) into the ink, and he did not say anything to me. When I came to רבי עקיבא, he forbade it to me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי מאיר really learned from both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר describes his own experience with each teacher: רבי ישמעאל allowed his ink practice, and רבי עקיבא forbade it. This shows he spent time as a student of both. That makes him the natural candidate to quote רבי ישמעאל before רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught (in a ברייתא), introducing a proof
iron sulfate, added to ink to make it darker and longer-lasting
ink
he forbade it to me

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers resolve the contradiction. שמואל says the praise was only to sharpen the students. רב נחמן בר יצחק says the wording was 'appear reasonable'. Also, the unnamed תלמיד is רבי מאיר, who studied under both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא.
steps.confusionAlert: The ink story is not being brought here for its own הלכה. Its only job in this step is to prove that רבי מאיר studied with both teachers.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Meir said:
When I was with Rabbi Yishmael
I used to put iron sulfate into the ink,
phrases.notes: This was the ink used to write a ספר תורה.

phrases.english: and he did not say anything to me.
When I came to Rabbi Akiva,
he forbade it to me.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 8's claim that רבי מאיר served both teachers.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר served both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי מאיר describes each teacher's response to his use of קנקנתום in ink.

steps.title: A different version of רבי מאיר's story reverses the order of his teachers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks 'Is that so?' and quotes רבי מאיר saying he first learned with רבי עקיבא and later came to רבי ישמעאל, who warned him to be careful as a סופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, quoting רבי מאיר: When I learned with רבי עקיבא, I used to put קנקנתום into my ink, and he said nothing to me. When I came to רבי ישמעאל, he asked me: My son, what is your work? I said: I am a scribe. He told me: My son, be careful in your work, because it is holy work. If you leave out even one letter or add even one letter, you could end up destroying the whole world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא it just brought in Step 9. It quotes another source where רבי מאיר describes his two teachers in the opposite order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier ברייתא, רבי מאיר learned first with רבי ישמעאל and then with רבי עקיבא. Here he says he was first with רבי עקיבא and only afterward 'came to' רבי ישמעאל. So which teacher came first? The story continues in the next step, where it also becomes clear which teacher objected to the ink.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that so?!' A formula that opens a challenge from another source.
Iron sulfate (vitriol). A substance added to ink so it sticks firmly and is hard to erase.
Ink
A scribe who writes ספרי תורה
Holy work, work done for Heaven

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge has two parts. One is the ORDER of רבי מאיר's teachers. The other is WHICH teacher objected to the קנקנתום. Step 14 names both contradictions. Step 15 resolves the order, and step 16 leaves the question of who forbade it unanswered.

phrases.english: Is that so?!
phrases.notes: Signals a contradiction from another source.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda say in the name of Shmuel, quoting Rabbi Meir:
When I was learning with Rabbi Akiva
I used to put iron sulfate into the ink,
and he did not say anything to me.
And when I came to Rabbi Yishmael,
he said to me: My son, what is your work?
I said to him: I am a scribe.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי: בְּנִי, הֱוֵי זָהִיר בִּמְלַאכְתֶּךָ,
phrases.english: He said to me: My son, be careful in your work,
for your work is the work of Heaven,
perhaps you will leave out one letter
or add one extra letter —

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצֵאתָ מַחֲרִיב אֶת כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ.
phrases.english: you will end up destroying the entire world.
phrases.notes: One letter can change the meaning of a word, for example אמת (truth) becoming מת (death).

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא in Step 9 with a conflicting account of רבי מאיר's teachers.
steps.kashyaTarget: The Step 9 ברייתא's account of the order in which רבי מאיר studied with רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second source from רבי מאיר himself puts רבי עקיבא first and רבי ישמעאל second, the reverse of the ברייתא. It will also show רבי ישמעאל objecting to the ink, not רבי עקיבא. Both accounts cannot be accurate as stated.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל objects to putting קנקנתום in the ink
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר tells רבי ישמעאל that he uses קנקנתום. רבי ישמעאל objects, citing the סוטה verse 'וכתב ומחה', which requires writing that can be erased.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to him: I have one thing called קנקנתום that I put into the ink. He said to me: Do people put קנקנתום into ink? Doesn't the תורה say 'and he shall write and erase'? It must be writing that can be erased.
steps.whatsHappening: The quoted story continues. Here רבי ישמעאל is the one who objects to the ink, the opposite of the earlier ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier version, the teacher who forbade קנקנתום was רבי עקיבא. Here it is רבי ישמעאל. His proof comes from the פרשת סוטה, where the curses are written and then washed off into water. Ink that cannot be erased would not work for that.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he shall write and erase.' The סוטה verse in במדבר ה:כג
Writing that is able to be erased
A woman suspected of adultery, whose test includes erasing written curses into water

phrases.aramaic: אָמַרְתִּי לוֹ: דָּבָר אֶחָד יֵשׁ לִי
phrases.english: I said to him: I have one thing

phrases.aramaic: וְ׳קַנְקַנְתּוֹם׳ שְׁמוֹ, שֶׁאֲנִי מֵטִיל לְתוֹךְ הַדְּיוֹ.
phrases.english: called 'iron sulfate,' which I put into the ink.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי: וְכִי מְטִילִין קַנְקַנְתּוֹם לְתוֹךְ הַדְּיוֹ?
phrases.english: He said to me: Does one put iron sulfate into ink?
But doesn't the Torah say: 'And he shall write and erase,'
meaning writing that can be erased.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַרְתִּי לוֹ: דָּבָר אֶחָד יֵשׁ לִי וְ׳קַנְקַנְתּוֹם׳ שְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted source that makes up the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: Which teacher forbade קנקנתום in the Step 9 ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here רבי ישמעאל forbids the ink, while the earlier version says רבי עקיבא forbade it. This deepens the contradiction about the order and roles of the teachers.

steps.title: How does רבי מאיר's reply answer רבי ישמעאל's warning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pauses to ask how mentioning ink answers a warning about adding or leaving out letters.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was he telling him, and what was he answering him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the main challenge to ask a side question about the story itself. It is setting up an explanation of the conversation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל warned about spelling errors, meaning missing or extra letters. רבי מאיר answered about ink. That seems unrelated, since ink does not stop a scribe from misspelling.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What was he saying to him?' Asks what a statement means
Answers him, replies to him

phrases.english: What was he saying to him,
and what was he answering him?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָאֲמַר לֵיהּ, וּמַאי קָא מְהַדַּר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side clarification about the story quoted in the challenge.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי מאיר's mention of קנקנתום answers a warning about missing or extra letters

steps.title: רבי מאיר means his ink protects even against a fly smudging a letter
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר meant: I am an expert, so spelling mistakes are not a concern. I even guard against a fly smudging the corner of a ד and turning it into a ר, because my ink contains קנקנתום.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he told him: I certainly don't make mistakes with missing or extra letters, because I am an expert. I am even careful about a fly. It might land on the corner of a ד, smudge it, and turn it into a ר. For that, I have one thing called קנקנתום that I put into the ink.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the conversation. רבי מאיר skipped over spelling errors because he was an expert, and answered an even smaller worry instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference between ד and ר is the small corner, the תג. If wet ink smudges there, a ד becomes a ר and a word changes. For example, אחד in שמע ישראל could become אחר. קנקנתום makes the ink stick firmly, so such smudging cannot happen.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It goes without saying.' Introduces an obvious case before a bigger one
Words spelled without or with an extra letter (missing or added letters)
Expert, well-versed
Fly
The corner (crown) of the letter ד
The letter ר

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר's ink was not about spelling. It protected the letters from accidental smudging. The גמרא now returns to the main challenge. Step 14 lists the two contradictions: the order of his teachers and who forbade the ink. Step 15 resolves the first, and Step 16 leaves the second unanswered.

phrases.english: This is what he was saying to him:
It goes without saying regarding missing and extra letters [that I do not make mistakes] —
since I am an expert,
but even the concern about a fly as well,
that perhaps it will come and sit on the corner of a dalet
and smudge it and make it into a reish —

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר אֶחָד יֵשׁ לִי וְקַנְקַנְתּוֹם שְׁמוֹ
phrases.english: I have one thing called iron sulfate
which I put into the ink.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא מִיבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the side question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר was saying that spelling errors are no concern for an expert like him, and even the rare danger of a fly smudging a ד into a ר is prevented by his קנקנתום ink.

steps.title: Two contradictions between the two reports
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out two clashes between the ברייתא and the report of רבי מאיר's own words. One is about the order of his teachers. The other is about who forbade קנקנתום.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a contradiction about whom he served, and there is a contradiction about who forbade it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the two sources side by side and names two places where they disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says רבי מאיר was first with רבי ישמעאל and that רבי עקיבא forbade קנקנתום. The report of רבי מאיר's own words says he was first with רבי עקיבא and that רבי ישמעאל objected. So both the order of his teachers and the identity of the one who forbade it are reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; a contradiction
Serving and studying under a teacher
He forbade it (the קנקנתום)
Against; one source set against the other

steps.confusionAlert: Both clashes run in opposite directions. In the ברייתא, רבי ישמעאל comes first and רבי עקיבא forbids. In the report of רבי מאיר's own words, רבי עקיבא comes first and רבי ישמעאל objects.

phrases.english: There is a difficulty between service and service,
phrases.notes: Which teacher did רבי מאיר serve first?

phrases.english: there is a difficulty between 'he forbade it' and 'he forbade it.'
phrases.notes: Who forbade קנקנתום: רבי עקיבא or רבי ישמעאל?

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא שִׁימּוּשׁ אַשִּׁימּוּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining what רבי מאיר meant by mentioning ink, the גמרא returns to the 'Is that so?' challenge and lays out the contradictions.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the ברייתא's account fits with the report of רבי מאיר's own words
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two sources reverse both the order of the teachers and which teacher forbade קנקנתום.

steps.title: Resolving the order of teachers
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר started with רבי עקיבא but could not follow him. He went to רבי ישמעאל to learn the basic tradition, then returned to רבי עקיבא to learn reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The contradiction about whom he served is no problem. At first he came to רבי עקיבא. Since he could not keep up with him, he went to רבי ישמעאל and learned the basic tradition. Then he came back to רבי עקיבא and learned deeper reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first contradiction by showing that both sources are true. רבי מאיר was with each teacher at different stages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's own report describes his very first stay with רבי עקיבא. The ברייתא describes the later sequence, from רבי ישמעאל back to רבי עקיבא. Once he had the basics from רבי ישמעאל, he could understand רבי עקיבא's analysis.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted; this part is fine (a 'but' usually follows)
At first; originally
To grasp his view; to keep up with his reasoning
He learned the received tradition (the basic material)
He learned logical analysis (the reasoning)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common way of learning: first master the basic tradition, then go deeper into the reasoning.

phrases.english: Granted, service against service is not difficult:
at first he came before Rabbi Akiva,
and since he could not grasp his reasoning,

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, וּגְמַר גְּמָרָא,
phrases.english: he came before Rabbi Yishmael and learned the tradition,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲדַר אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, וּסְבַר סְבָרָא.
phrases.english: and then came back before Rabbi Akiva and learned reasoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא שִׁימּוּשׁ אַשִּׁימּוּשׁ לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first of the two contradictions raised in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonization: each source describes a different stage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that רבי מאיר served the two teachers in only one order.
steps.terutzMaskana: He went from רבי עקיבא to רבי ישמעאל and back to רבי עקיבא, so both orders are true.

steps.title: The question of who forbade the ink stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction about who forbade קנקנתום remains. The גמרא admits that it has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the contradiction about who forbade it is still difficult! Indeed, it is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states that the second contradiction is not solved and leaves it as an open difficulty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving between teachers explains the order. It does not explain why one source says רבי עקיבא forbade קנקנתום and the other says רבי ישמעאל did. The single word קַשְׁיָא at the end is the verdict: the difficulty stands unanswered.

keyTerms.meaning: But; however (turns to the part that is still a problem)
First a question ('it is difficult!'), then a verdict ('indeed it remains difficult')

steps.whatToRemember: The order of רבי מאיר's teachers is resolved: he went back and forth. Who forbade קנקנתום is left as an unanswered קשיא.
steps.confusionAlert: The second קַשְׁיָא is not a repeat of the question. It is the גמרא's final verdict that no answer was found.

phrases.english: But 'he forbade it' against 'he forbade it' is difficult!
It is indeed difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֲסָרָהּ אַאֲסָרָהּ קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After solving the first contradiction, the גמרא returns to the second one and leaves it open.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The contradiction over who forbade קנקנתום has no answer.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's rule: קנקנתום is allowed in ink except for the סוטה passage
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי מאיר: קנקנתום may be added to ink for all holy writing except פרשת סוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה says that רבי מאיר used to say, 'For everything we may put קנקנתום into the ink, except for the סוטה passage.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about where קנקנתום may be used. This continues the topic of the ink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קנקנתום makes ink permanent, so it is fine for all holy writing. The סוטה passage is the exception because it must be erasable ('וכתב ומחה'). This fits what רבי ישמעאל said earlier about erasing.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
We may put in; we may add
Iron sulfate (vitriol), which makes ink hard to erase
Ink
The Torah passage about the סוטה, written and then erased in water

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says,
Rabbi Meir used to say:
for all writings, we may put iron sulfate into the ink,
except for the passage of the sotah.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָיָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the unresolved contradiction and brings a related ברייתא about the ink.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קנקנתום may be added to ink for all holy writing except פרשת סוטה.

steps.title: A narrower version: only the סוטה scroll used in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב reports רבי מאיר's view differently. Only the סוטה passage actually used in the מקדש is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב says in רבי מאיר's name: except for the סוטה passage that is used in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: A second version of רבי מאיר's rule narrows the exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יעקב's version, the only text that cannot have קנקנתום is the סוטה passage written for the actual ceremony in the מקדש, because that one gets erased. The סוטה passage inside a regular ספר תורה is never erased, so it may be written with קנקנתום like everything else.

keyTerms.meaning: In his name (here, in רבי מאיר's name)
That is in the מקדש; the text used for the actual ceremony

steps.whyThisMatters: The two versions disagree on whether the exception covers every written copy of the סוטה passage or only the copy that will actually be erased.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ya'akov says in his name:
except for the sotah passage that is in the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר מִשְּׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the same ruling, with a narrower exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the סוטה passage written for the ceremony in the מקדש may not have קנקנתום.

steps.title: What practical difference is there between the two versions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the first ברייתא and רבי יעקב's report of רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what real-life difference there is between the two reports of רבי מאיר's view. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One version says קנקנתום is allowed for all holy writing except פרשת סוטה. The other says only the סוטה passage actually used in the מקדש is excluded. The גמרא wants to know when these two versions would give different rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? (A standard question asking for the practical difference between two views.)

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: Refers to the two versions of רבי מאיר's view from steps 17 and 18.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical difference between the two reports just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what case do the two versions of רבי מאיר's view lead to different rulings?

steps.title: The difference is erasing the passage from a ספר תורה
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה says the two versions disagree about whether the סוטה passage in a ספר תורה may be erased for a סוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה said: The difference between them is whether one may erase it from the ספר תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ירמיה answers that the two versions differ about whether the סוטה passage written in a ספר תורה may be erased into the water for a סוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the first version, the passage in a ספר תורה could be erased for a סוטה. So even a Torah scroll must write that passage without קנקנתום, because that ink does not erase. Under רבי יעקב's version, the Torah's passage cannot be used for a סוטה. So only a special סוטה scroll must avoid קנקנתום.

keyTerms.meaning: To erase. A סוטה scroll is erased into the bitter waters.
From a ספר תורה, meaning the סוטה passage written inside it.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the קנקנתום question really depends on a deeper question: can a Torah scroll serve as the סוטה scroll?

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya said:
to erase it from the Torah scroll
phrases.notes: Erasing the סוטה passage from a Torah scroll for the woman's water.

phrases.english: is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה: לִמְחוֹק לָהּ מִן הַתּוֹרָה אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two versions differ about whether the סוטה passage may be erased from a ספר תורה.

steps.title: This matches an older dispute about reusing a סוטה scroll
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the same dispute appears in a ברייתא: can a scroll written for one סוטה be used for another סוטה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And these תנאים are like those תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches: Her scroll is not fit to give another סוטה to drink with it. רבי אחי בר יאשיה says: Her scroll is fit to give another סוטה to drink with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that the dispute about erasing from a ספר תורה is the same as an older dispute. That older dispute asks whether a scroll written for one סוטה may be used for a different סוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shared question seems to be whether the scroll must be written for this specific woman. The תנא קמא says it must, so another woman's scroll is unfit. This matches רבי יעקב's version, where a Torah scroll cannot be used. רבי אחי בר יאשיה allows it, which matches the first version, where a Torah scroll can be erased.

keyTerms.meaning: And these תנאים are like those תנאים. The גמרא is linking one dispute to another.
Her scroll: the סוטה passage written for a specific woman.
To give to drink: to prepare the bitter waters for her.
A different סוטה, not the woman the scroll was written for.

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the matching straight. The תנא קמא (not fit) goes with רבי יעקב (do not erase from a Torah). רבי אחי בר יאשיה (fit) goes with the first version (may erase from a Torah).

phrases.english: And these tanna'im are like those tanna'im,
as it was taught: Her scroll is not fit
to give another sota to drink with it.
Rabbi Achai bar Yoshiya says:
Her scroll is fit
to give another sota to drink with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי תַנָּאֵי כִי הָנֵי תַנָּאֵי, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links רב ירמיה's practical difference to an older dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That the dispute about erasing from a ספר תורה is the same as an already known dispute.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about reusing one סוטה's scroll for another סוטה.

steps.title: רב פפא: the תנא קמא might still allow using a ספר תורה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא argues that the תנא קמא forbids reusing a scroll only because it was already set aside for a different woman. A ספר תורה was written for no one in particular, so he might allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Perhaps that is not so. The תנא קמא only said his ruling there because once a scroll was set aside for רחל, it cannot later be set aside for לאה. But a ספר תורה is written without any person in mind, so he too may agree that we erase it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back on the matching from step 21. He shows that the תנא קמא does not have to agree with רבי יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא's problem may be that the scroll was already tied to a different woman. It is not that the scroll was never written for this woman. A Torah scroll was written neutrally, so it is not tied to anyone, and even the תנא קמא could allow erasing it.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps it is not so. A formula used to reject a proposed comparison.
He only said his ruling in that case. It limits a view to its original setting.
It was designated for (literally 'set apart in the name of') someone.
It is written without anyone in particular in mind.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Perhaps it is not so.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר תַּנָּא קַמָּא הָתָם —
phrases.english: The first tanna only said his ruling there
because, since it was designated for Rachel,
phrases.notes: Rachel and Leah are sample names for two different women.

phrases.aramaic: תּוּ לָא הָדְרָא מִינַּתְקָא לְשׁוּם לֵאָה,
phrases.english: it can no longer be designated for Leah.
But regarding a Torah scroll, which is written without anyone in mind,
he too may agree that we erase it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: דִּילְמָא לָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the matching of the תנא קמא with רבי יעקב.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the matching from the תנא קמא's side.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The תנא קמא's reason may be that the scroll was already tied to another woman. That reason does not apply to a neutral Torah scroll.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: רבי אחי might still forbid using a ספר תורה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק argues that רבי אחי בר יאשיה allows reusing a scroll only because it was at least written for some סוטה. A ספר תורה was written for study, so he might forbid erasing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Perhaps that is not so. רבי אחי בר יאשיה only said his ruling there because the scroll was at least written for some סוטה in the world. But a ספר תורה is written for learning, so he too may agree that we do not erase it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק attacks the matching from the other side. He shows that רבי אחי בר יאשיה does not have to agree with the first version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אחי may allow reuse only because the scroll was written for the purpose of a סוטה, even if for a different woman. A Torah scroll was written for study, not for a סוטה at all. So even רבי אחי could forbid erasing it, and the matching fails on this side too.

keyTerms.meaning: At least.
It was written for learning, not for a סוטה.
We erase.

steps.whatToRemember: רב ירמיה ties the קנקנתום question to whether a ספר תורה may be erased for a סוטה. The attempt to match this to the dispute over reusing a סוטה scroll is pushed back from both sides. The two disputes may be independent.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Perhaps it is not so.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אַחַי בַּר יֹאשִׁיָּה הָתָם —
phrases.english: Rabbi Achai bar Yoshiya only said his ruling there

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא דְּאִיכְּתִיב מִיהַת לְשׁוּם סוֹטָה בָּעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: because it was at least written for some sota in the world.
But regarding a Torah scroll, which is written for learning,
he too may agree that we do not erase it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, דִּילְמָא לָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second rejection, this time from רבי אחי בר יאשיה's side, completing the push-back against step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The matching from רבי אחי בר יאשיה's side.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אחי's leniency may depend on the scroll being written for a סוטה purpose, which a Torah scroll written for study lacks.

steps.title: Starting a challenge from the case of a divorce document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins asking whether רבי אחי בר יאשיה disagrees with a known משנה about a גט written to divorce one's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי אחי בר יאשיה not accept what we learned in a משנה: "If a man wrote a גט to divorce his wife,"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge against רבי אחי בר יאשיה by starting to quote a משנה about a גט. The rest of the משנה, and the actual point of the challenge, comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אחי בר יאשיה allows a scroll written for one סוטה to be used for another סוטה. The גמרא now brings in the laws of גט, where a document must be written for a specific woman. The challenge will be: if a גט written for one wife cannot be used for another, why should a סוטה scroll be any different?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Following the discussion of רבי אחי בר יאשיה's view that a סוטה scroll may be reused for another woman, the גמרא now challenges that view from the laws of גט.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אחי בר יאשיה's ruling that a scroll written for one סוטה may be used for another סוטה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה about גט requires that the document be written for a specific woman. This suggests that writing for one woman does not work for another, which seems to contradict רבי אחי בר יאשיה. The full contradiction appears once the rest of the משנה is quoted.
